lines: PRESIDENT:  Before we continue with the witness, I would
like to comment.
I just would like to say that I understand that
a representative of each party is keeping a record of
how much time has been used by each counsel in
examination of witnesses and how much time they have
remaining according to the chess clock.
So please, could you provide the tribunal with an
update on how much time has been used so far by each
counsel, and how much time they each have remaining.
Tell us, Mr Burke, if you can indicate, how long you
will take in total to examine all of the respondent's
factual witness, to check how much time is left for
you for today.  This is number 1.
Number 2, which is very important.  I would like
to remind counsel that they should aim to be efficient
in their examination of witnesses.  So there is no
need to repeat the same question again and again,
especially where the witness's answer is unlikely to
change.
The last point I would like to emphasise, that it
is very important for the counsel to examine all
witnesses in a respectful manner and ensure an
appropriate tone is maintained in all exchanges with
the witnesses.
The requirement to demonstrate courtesy and
respect is also stated in the LCIA's EDI guidance, and
I ask counsel to be mindful of that.
Is that okay with both counsel?
MR BURKE:  Yes, sir.
I don't have -- so I have the running totals of
the amount of time that we've had, which I understand
was agreed as of the first two days; it was agreed
this morning.
What I don't have in front of me is the time
remaining.  So someone will have to do the maths in
order to do that.
But the running totals, my understanding, were
agreed as of last night.  The claimant has had
227 minutes, the respondent has had 317 minutes.  And
then there is the balance, which is attributable to
tribunal time or the IT issue that we had yesterday
with the transcript.
In terms of my intention for today, my strong hope
is that I can finish with the respondent's factual
witnesses today.  There is a chance that one may go to
tomorrow.
Given that we are ahead of schedule and we'll see
how we go, it might make sense not to start him and
finish him completely tomorrow, rather than have him
on and then have him in purdah overnight.  But I think
we should see how we get on.
I did have in the timetable slightly more than
a day and a half for cross-examination of the factual
witnesses allocated, so I will be coming in under
budget if I complete within that time frame.
PRESIDENT:  Well, thank you very much, Mr Burke, for
that.
The purpose here, as you know, is to give equal
time for both counsel to re-examine the other, and how
you utilise your time, the total time -- I don't know,
is it my understanding that there's kind of reference
for like three hours for each counsel for factual
witness?
MR BURKE:  I'm sorry, sir, could you repeat the question?
PRESIDENT:  Is there any agreement somehow that for each
counsel to spend three hours to re-examine?
MR BURKE:  No.  I think the agreement was to an
indicative timetable for how we were to use our time,
but that ultimately it would be for us to use the
equal allocation of time as we saw fit, obviously
subject to the tribunal's control.
The running order, or the order of play at least,
has been such that we are ahead of schedule.  I think
we are about a day ahead of schedule, and having
deferred the quantum evidence, that means I think we
are in no danger of not finishing on Friday.  I would
imagine that we will get through most of the --
certainly my delay expert tomorrow, and we may even
get to the respondent's delay expert tomorrow as well.
So I'm certainly confident, for my part at least,
that we will be comfortably finished on Friday.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you for that.
Respondent counsel, you would like to comment
before we give opportunity for the tribunal member?
Do you have any comments before we start?
MR WYGAS:  No.  No, sir, I don't need to comment.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
My co-arbitrators, you would like to?
DR TALEB:  I'm fine.  Thank you.
MR COLE:  Yeah, no comment, thank you.
PRESIDENT:  Excellent.  Now, can we call the --
MR BURKE:  I just have, sorry, two short housekeeping
points.  One is to your point, sir, right at the very
beginning of the hearing with regard to the current
situation in the Middle East.
I understand from press reports and from speaking
to my client, who is in Bahrain, that there were some
missile strikes overnight or there were some missile
attacks overnight.  I just wanted to make sure that
everyone was able to continue today, given what seems
to have been an escalation overnight.
PRESIDENT:  Well, this I will leave for my colleague,
Dr Abdulla.
DR TALEB:  Yeah.  Actually, last night between 2.00 and
3.00 am, yes, there was some missiles attacked in
Bahrain, and not far from my house.  But I think this
all taken around 20 to 25 minutes.  It was just that
incident and things are okay.  Everything is open.
Probably Bahrain airport, the airspace was closed for
a couple of hours.
PRESIDENT:  Yes.
DR TALEB:  Maybe for four hours.  Then it was reopened.
I think things are, Alhamdulillah, things are okay.
Thank you so much.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.  Thank you.
MR BURKE:  Just one final point, sir.  Sorry.
PRESIDENT:  No, no, no.  I would say safety comes first.
So if at any point, if any tribunal member or the
witness or the counsel feel they want to adjourn for
the security purpose, of course we have to adjourn.
Thank you.
MR BURKE:  And the only other point, sir, is we received
overnight, and I saw them for the first time this
morning, under cover of an errata to Mr Prasad's first
witness statement, 27 new exhibits.
We've had no explanation as to why new exhibits
are being introduced by way of errata.  I have only
seen them myself very briefly this morning.  I am,
certainly pending an explanation as to why they're now
being introduced, going to reserve my position.  We
won't get to Mr Prasad until after the next break, and
I will have an opportunity to review them then, but
I certainly would appreciate some explanation of why
27 new documents have been introduced by way of
errata.
PRESIDENT:  Mr Wygas, you would like to comment now or
leave it later?
MR WYGAS:  The documents, on a final review of the
statement, it was found that the documents that were
referred to were not the right ones and these are the
right exhibits.  It's as simple as that.
PRESIDENT:  All right, thank you.
MR WYGAS:  Actually, all they are is 27 individual
photographs.  They're not in any way voluminous.  It's
not 1,868 documents.
PRESIDENT:  All right.  Thank you for that.
So without any further ado, can we call the
witness, please?
MR BURKE:  Thank you, sir.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.  Yes.
MR WYGAS:  Maybe if Lloyd Michaux could let Mr Varghese
in.
MR KULACHITYAL MATHAI VARGHESE (continued)
WITNESS:  Good morning to everyone.
PRESIDENT:  Good morning, Mr Varghese.
WITNESS:  Hi.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.  I just want to remind you again,
you are still under affirmation or under oath.
WITNESS:  Yes.
PRESIDENT:  Thank you.
Cross-examination by MR BURKE (continued)
MR BURKE:  Mr Varghese, good morning.
Is it possible to tilt your camera down at all?
You're quite low in the frame.
Thank you.  That's somewhat better.
Mr Varghese, are you still alone in the room?
A. Yes, yes.
Q. Have you spoken to anybody about this case overnight?
A. No.
Q. Thank you.
Could we please put up {E2447}.
Yes, thank you.
Mr Varghese, you will recognise this, I'm sure, as
your letter of 21st November 2023.
If we scroll down to the bottom of that page, we
can see actually every page of this is signed by you.
Do you see that?
A. Yes.
Q. Do you recognise this letter?
A. Sorry?
Q. Do you recognise this letter?  Do you know what this
letter is?
A. Yes.
Q. What is it?
A. What is this about?  The notice of termination, the
answer to that one.
Q. Yes.
A. On which basis the welfare, the contract was
terminated because we were having all the things.
That is why we given the answer.
Q. So this is your response, this is Down Town's response
to TTSJV's notice of termination of 20th November,
correct?
A. Yes, yes.
Q. Yes.  We'll look at a couple of things that you say in
this letter in a few moments.
But if we could just look on the second page, so
{E2447}, and it's the last paragraph that the kind of
big block of text on the -- if we scroll down, please,
the bottom of the page.
So you say -- it's the paragraph that starts with
"Currently".  Do you see that?
A. Yeah.
Q. "Currently, the SUBCONTRACTOR is actively working in
Noga for cable trenches ..."
And then, middle of the page, or middle of that
paragraph, you say:
"... we are confident that we will be completing
our remaining scope of ongoing works as per the
attached program with the available current manpower
and with required machinery/equipment ..."
Do you see that?
A. Yeah.
Q. If we then look to page 4 of this letter, so
You may need to just rotate it.
This is the attached programme.  And if we zoom in
just at the top, the box at the top that says "Bapco
modernisation programme" in blue with yellow font.
A. Yeah.
Q. You can see that what you are proposing in the
schedule is that Down Town would finish its remaining
works by 31st January 2024.  Is that right?
A. No, it is -- you take for the January '24, then you
have got other sheets there.
Q. Yes.
A. Start of remaining works by 30th November '23.
Q. Yes.
A. You can see what is -- this is the programme what we
given to them.
Q. Yes.  But what the summary bar at the top is -- so
there's obviously the detail of the programme that
follows.
A. Yes.
Q. But the bar at the top, where it says start 30th
November '23, finish 31st January '24?
A. Yes.
Q. What you're saying to TTSJV is that if you are allowed
to continue, you would finish your remaining works by
31st January 2024.  Is that right?
A. Right.
Q. And you are saying that because you understood that
TTSJV's notice of termination was in part based on the
fact that TTSJV considered Down Town to be late?
Correct?
A. Down Town to be late in the sense, because I want to
bring to your kind attention that the contract was
expired on 31st August 2023.  We are allowed to
continue to work when the contract was expired, and
they asked us to extend our performance bond and
insurance covers and guarantees up to 31st December.
Then we have state in our earlier letters that we are
willing to extend our respective bonds or guarantees
up to 31st January 2024, they even don't want to talk
to us.
We have written two or three times to that.  They
say: finish the final account and talk.  How we can
talk to them without finishing the final account?
Because the job was ongoing.  Job was ongoing.  Even
though they terminated, we were doing some
over-pumping and other things up to 31st January 2024.
We have the proof, in sections and the gate passes
and all the things with us, we have forward it to our
legal counsel about it, that we have a proof that you
are allowed us to work up to January '24, other than
the concession works, because you don't have any
alternative, put any over pumping.  Otherwise all
Bapco should have been flooded that area.  That was
the main reason they allow us to work on that area.
But even they allow me to work on that area, why
they didn't allow us to work on the other area?
And again, I just want to bring to your notice
that, okay, the contract, why it terminated on
22nd November?  Why they did not do it on 30th August?
If you say that one, default of the contract are
coming up to 31st August, why they take this one up to
22nd November?  Because they want to --
PRESIDENT:  Mr Varghese, sorry, I have to interrupt you
here.
I remind you many times, please, keep your answer
very short to the question.  We don't need that much
of clarification unless the counsel ask you for
clarification, because we have a lot of witness we
have to go through today.
A. Okay, sir.  Sorry, sir.
PRESIDENT:  No, no, no, no sorry.  Just I want to be
efficient with your statement; otherwise we are
wasting our time here.
A. Okay, sir.
MR BURKE:  I don't expect you to agree with TTSJV that
you were late, but the reason you are telling TTSJV in
response to this termination notice that you will
complete by 31st January is because you knew, you
understood from the termination notice, that one of
the grounds for termination was that TTSJV thought
Down Town was late.  Correct?
A. No.  TTSJV's thought, I cannot --
PRESIDENT:  Mr Varghese, can you answer with "yes" or
"no"?  At least at this point.  Correct or not
correct?  Don't give too much explanation because then
you confuse everyone.
A. No.
MR BURKE:  So you did not understand the notice of
termination -- one of the reasons for termination to
be that Down Town was late.  Is that right?
A. Yeah.  That may be their assumption, because as far as
I know, it is no.
Q. Could we go back to page 1 of the letter, please.
What you are doing in this letter, I think you've
agreed with me already, is trying to persuade TTSJV
not to cancel the contract.  Correct?  The
subcontract?
A. Yes.
Q. Yes.  And so it was important that everything you said
in this letter was correct, yes?
A. Yes.
Q. If we look at the second -- you've got a number of
points, a number of numbered points.  If we could look
at number 2.
Just scroll down so we can have that in the middle
of the page.
We see you say:
"Delay in final settlement payment."
That's one of the things in the termination
notice.  And it says:
"The subcontractor has already started paying
final settlement and till now, more than 45 people
were paid and the proof of evidence already shared
with TTSJV."
Can you remember what and when that proof of
evidence was shared, Mr Varghese?  Was it your
8th October letter?
A. See, this one is after the termination.  What was the
current situation, we updated in this letter.  That is
correct.
Q. Mr Varghese, my question was slightly different.
You've said in this letter that you had already
shown or shared the proof that you'd paid 45 people's
final settlements.
A. Yeah.
Q. I'm asking if you can remember when and in what way
you had shared that proof with TTSJV.  Was it your
8th October letter?
A. Along with the letter, there will be acknowledgment
from the staff that when they received the payment.
That is there along with the letter.
Q. Okay.  So you think there is a letter with an
attachment somewhere that shows acknowledgment of
those people receiving their settlements?  Is that
your understanding?
A. Yeah.  That settlement and our finance man can provide
you more proof on that one with his statement, because
he has all the proof on the payment to the particular
staff or people or anyone.  He can answer to you that
one.
What I have been told, this has been paid.  That
is why I say this has been paid.
Either, another 20 people will be paid in
November.  As the contract has been terminated on
20th, that will be pre-paid end of the month.
Q. So --
A. Balance will be --
Q. Sorry, Mr Varghese, I guess I didn't mean to
interrupt.  Please.
So you are saying in this letter, 45 people had
already been paid?
A. Yeah.
Q. That's the first point.
The second point, that you were going to pay
another 20 people by the end of November?
A. Yeah.
Q. So within a couple of weeks of this letter.
A. Yeah.
Q. Correct?
A. Yeah.
Q. So those people have not been paid at the date of this
letter, correct?  Those 20 people?
A. Yes.
Q. Yes.  And then you are then saying the balance will be
paid before 30th December 2023.  So the rest of the
people who are awaiting their final settlements,
you're telling TTSJV that they'll be paid before the
end of 2023, before the end of the year; correct?
A. Yes.
Q. Do you remember -- and I'm just talking about a rough
figure here, not a specific figure -- how many people
you are talking about when you say "the balance"?
A. It's our accounts can answer it because they know it,
how many people paid, which are the people paid.
Q. Do you have a --
A. I don't know exactly how many people have been paid in
December.
Q. Could we look -- sorry.  I can help you, Mr Varghese,
and this is not a memory test.
Could we look at {E2474}.  This is your next
letter.
This is a further letter from you.  We can see,
I'm not sure whether you've signed every page of this,
but you've certainly signed the last one.
Actually, yes, if we scroll down to the bottom
page, we can see your signature on every page.
You see that you've signed that that document?
A. Yes.
Q. Yes?  Do you recognise this letter?
A. Yes.
Q. If we could go back up, please, to bullet point 2.
This is a reply to a TTSJV letter that's in
between the two letters we just looked at.  And you
say, number 2:
"The subcontractor already shared the details of
the employees who left the company with details.  The
total number of employees waiting for settlement is
268 and not 1000."
So does that sound right?  There were 268 people
as at the end of November 2023 who had not had their
final settlements paid; that's what you're saying
here, isn't it?
A. Yeah.
Q. If we go, please, back to -- do you know whether those
settlements were paid by the end of December 2023,
Mr Varghese?
A. Yes, as far as I have been told, it has been paid.
Settlements are paid.  If November settlement, will
not be paid in December, because the November card
will come by the site, by end of first week of
December --
Q. When you say -- sorry, I don't mean to interrupt.
When you say that you've been told that these
people had their final settlements paid, who told you
that, and when did they tell you that?
A. This accounts people.  On the date I written on the
letter, that date they told: this will be paid on
so-and-so.
Q. Do you have a name?  A particular -- an individual,
a human being who told you?
A. Yeah, individual will be paid.  And some of the people
already left and we are informed them: you can come
and collect the money.  And we arrange their address
and we call them, somebody coming from India, somebody
coming from UAE, somebody coming from -- what is
called -- Saudi Arabia to collect the money.
Q. Do you remember the name of the person in your finance
team who told you that those settlements had been paid
by the end of December?  It's okay if you don't.
A. Yeah.  Here, now, you can ask, the finance people also
change, but the current finance manager, that is the
chief accountant, can give it to you.  His name is
Bathusha.  He can answer to you which date it is
given.  His witness statement it may be stated.  He
can give you the answer to that one.
Q. Okay.  Was it him who would have told you at the time
or would it have been the former chief accountant?
A. Yes.
Q. Okay.  Can we please go back to the previous letter?
So this is {E2447}.
We can see number 1 now in the middle of the page:
"Delay in salary payment to employees."
You say:
"All pending salaries up to September 2023 month
has been paid by SUBCONTRACTOR.  The salary for the
month of October will be paid on or before 26th
November 2023."
Do you see that?
A. Yes.
Q. The October salaries, they should have been paid on or
before 10th November, shouldn't they?
A. No.  Because October salaries, as I told you, the time
sheet come from the site, it has been verified from so
many people from the site.  The respective foremans,
engineers and supervisors, then the project manager,
then it will come accounts.  They will check in the
computer system the punching, these people are
correctly punched or not.  Then it takes some time.
Usually salaries are paid between 15th to 20th of
every month.  Sometimes, if this comes early, we pay
on or before 10th.
Q. Don't employment contracts for Down Town workers say
they're entitled to be paid on or before the 10th of
every month, Mr Varghese?
A. Yes.
Q. I'm sure you have your employment contract.
A. Yeah, you are right there.  But sometimes it get
delayed from the documents coming from the site, and
the verification will take some time.  But one or two
occasions only we have paid little late on the salary.
Particularly on otherwise we are paid on the due date,
one days plus or minus, according to that one.  Maybe
holidays falling in the 10th, maybe they have been
paid a Friday, it's Thursday it's coming.  Maybe
Friday, Saturday holiday.  Maybe Sunday it will have
been paid, two or three days' delay here and there.
That is answer to that point.
Q. Is that your evidence, Mr Varghese, that the only
delays to any worker salaries on this project were one
or two days because of a weekend, or because the time
cards took a while to be processed?  Is that your
evidence?
A. Yes.  You have the evidence.  The accounts man can
give it to you, this evidence.
Q. Do you believe that to be true, Mr Varghese?
A. According to the information I received, it is true.
Q. Information from whom?  From the accounts team?
A. From the accounts department.
Q. You are saying in this letter, this is at {E2447}, you
are telling the TTSJV, in an effort to avoid them
canceling your contract, that the salaries for October
were going to be paid on 26th November, weren't you?
A. Yeah.
Q. Were they paid on 26th November?
A. Yes.
Q. Shall we go --
A. That is what -- that is what is I have been told
later, all the pending salaries up to October has been
paid in November.
Q. You were told that all salaries for the month of
October --
A. Yeah.
Q. -- had in fact been paid on or before 26th November?
Is that your evidence?
A. Yes.  The evidence, our finance man can give it to
you.  In his witness statement, he might have stated.
I don't know, I did not see his witness statement.
None of the witness statement is shown to me.  They
independently prepare it and send to the counsel.
Counsel readjusted and given to, submitted by these
people.  Again, verification, and that is there.
You can ask our finance man that it is paid and he
will have the evidence, either gone to the bank or by
cash.
Q. Mr Varghese, I'm not asking what your finance manager
thought.  I'm asking what you understood.
A. I understood it is paid on or before 26th November.
Q. Could we look, please, then at your further letter,
So if we scroll to the top of this, we can see the
date of this letter is 27th November, yes?
A. Yes.
Q. This is, I appreciate, a stupid question, but
27th November is after 26th November, isn't it?
A. See, when 26th we say, that means we can pay up to
26th, then only we'll write the letter on 27th.
Without paying that one, how we can write the letter
26th: salaries are paid.  On or before --
Q. Mr Varghese, my question was -- I won't ask it again.
If we look at number 1, if we just scroll down so
we can see bullet point 1, we can see you're now
telling TTSJV on 27th November.
So the day after you've just said you believe the
salaries had already been paid --
A. Yeah.
Q. -- you are saying:
"All pending salaries up to September 2023 has
been paid by SUBCONTRACTOR."
A. Yeah.
Q. "The salary for the month of October is already
processed --"
A. Yeah.
Q. "-- which is being credited to worker's account."
A. Yeah.
Q. So what you're saying here is: the salaries haven't
been paid yet, but they've been processed to be paid.
Is that right?
A. If the letter says salaries all have been processed
and which is credited to the workers' account, means
salaries are paid by 26th.  That is the meaning of
that word.
Q. That's your evidence.  So you're actually more
emphatic than saying -- sorry, you're more clear than
you are saying that they're just processed.  You're
saying that means they have in fact been paid --
A. Yes.
Q. -- on 26th November?
A. Yes, yes, you are right.  It has been credited to
their account.
Q. And you know that because your finance team told you
that?
A. Yeah.  Our accounts department told us that one, it
had been processed and credited to the account,
workers' account.
Q. They told you it had actually been paid into the
relevant people's accounts, yes?
A. Yes.  Workers' account, or they collected as cash, who
has some problem with their credit -- ATM cards or CPR
cards.  It is they paid cash also there by 26th.
Q. Could we then go, please, to {E3342}.
Actually, just before we do.  Presumably, because
of your answer, you understood that Down Town had the
money available to pay those salaries.  They wouldn't
have been paid if Down Town didn't have the money in
its bank account to pay them; correct?
A. Yes.
Q. Thank you.
Could we then go to {E3342}, please.
We looked at these yesterday and we're going to
look slightly further on.  You'll recognise these
documents from yesterday afternoon, Mr Varghese?
A. Yes, we've seen it.  I answered to your point
yesterday itself to clarify this situation.
Q. Yes.
A. Yesterday --
Q. If we could please go to page 37, so {E3342}, page 37.
We can see these are the payroll instructions from
Down Town to its bank, to AUB Bank.  Yes?
A. Yeah.
Q. And these are for the salaries for the month of
October.  Do you see that?
A. Yeah.
Q. So these are the salaries we're just talking about,
the salaries that you say, your understanding was, had
in fact been paid into the workers' accounts --
A. Yes.
Q. -- on 26th October.  These are the salaries we're
talking about, yes?
A. Not October.  26th November we say.  Not October.
Q. Yes.  But you're talking about the October salaries.
We can go back and look at the letter, if you want.
A. October salary means it is paid in November only.  We
have already written in our earlier letter, say:
salary up to October has been paid or released by 26th
November.
Q. Yes.
A. And we say, we wrote to you on 27th saying that the
salary up to October has been paid or credited to that
account.
Q. Yes.  No, you said that the October salaries had been
paid, didn't you?
A. Yes.  October salaries are paid on or before 26th
November, as per our letter.  On salaries paid, the
information was given to me.  Then 27th, the next day,
we wrote the letter that salaries up to October has
been paid.
Q. Yes.  So if we look, so these are the October
salaries, they're the salaries we were just talking
about.  If we could just scroll down, we can see
again -- I think this page is very clear.
No, no, sorry -- actually, it doesn't matter.
They're on both pages.
We can see the date stamp right at the bottom of
that page.
If we scroll in.
You agreed with me yesterday that these date
stamps were the dates that the bank at least processed
the payroll instructions.  We can see that this
payroll instruction was not processed, was not
received by Down Town's bank until 26th December 2023,
can't we?
A. This the bank seal, this side on, I don't have any
proof to that one.  As you've shown it, it may be
correct, but you can see a signature down there.  The
senior accountant.  It's say 19/11.  19th of 11th,
they've given the paper to me that it has been already
given to the bank up to October salary.  Means what
I should assume, that it has been processed.
Q. So your evidence is that the big clear stamp in the
middle of this page where it says received by your
bank, that means something other than this is the date
it was received by the bank?  Is that your evidence?
A. Sir, bank, maybe you are right, because we sent to the
bank on that day.  Maybe there was some problem there
in the account, as we've not been credited by the
other ministries to our account.  Maybe bank sign this
one, acknowledge that one when they have the money in
the account.  That's maybe the reason.
